<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a Go-based, open-source library (not a standalone service) for building interactive, accessible forms and prompts in the terminal (“huh?”), plus a companion spinner sub-package.  
   - Key use cases:  
     • Standalone CLI prompts and forms  
     • Integration into Bubble Tea TUI apps  
     • Accessibility mode for screen readers  
     • The spinner for background activity indicators  

2. High-Level Structure Analysis  
   - Top-level packages and files:  
     • `accessibility.go` / `internal/accessibility`: core accessibility logic  
     • `form.go`, `group.go`, individual `field_*.go` files: the form builder API  
     • `option.go`, `selector`, `layout.go`, `validate.go`: field option management, rendering layout, validation  
     • `run.go`: main orchestration of the interactive prompt loop  
     • `theme.go`: theming abstraction (Lip Gloss based)  
     • `spinner/`: standalone spinner package with its own Go module  
     • `examples/`: client code demonstrating usage patterns  
     • Config/build: `go.mod`, `Makefile`, GitHub workflows, lint config  

3. Key Components to Represent in the Diagram  
   A. Core Library (“huh” package)  
     - Form Builder Layer  
       • Form  
       • Group  
       • Field types (Input, Text, Select, MultiSelect, Confirm)  
     - Option & Selector Layer  
       • Option  
       • internal/selector  
     - Layout & Rendering  
       • layout.go  
       • internal/accessibility (accessible fallback renderer)  
       • theme.go (Lip Gloss styling)  
     - Validation & State  
       • validate.go  
       • run.go (form lifecycle: Init, Update, View loop)  
   B. Spinner Sub-Package (`huh/spinner`)  
     - Spinner core  
     - Spinner examples  
   C. Examples (clients demonstrating forms, dynamic forms, Bubble Tea integration)  
   D. External Dependencies  
     - Bubble Tea (TUI framework)  
     - Lip Gloss (styling)  
     - Go standard library  
     - Any other 3rd-party libs defined in go.mod  

4. Relationships and Data Flow  
   - User’s Program → imports → Core Library  
   - Core Library:  
     • Orchestrates Form → Groups → Fields → Options  
     • On Run(): form.Run() → run.go triggers rendering cycle → layout + theme + accessibility → update user input → field state updates → validation  
   - Bubble Tea Integration: Form implements `tea.Model` → integrates into Bubble Tea’s Update/View  
   - Spinner: distinct module invoked post-form to show background work  

5. Architectural Patterns and Principles  
   - Modular design by feature (fields, layout, theme, accessibility)  
   - Separation of concerns: core logic vs. rendering vs. accessibility  
   - Plugin-style theming (strategies via theme.go)  
   - Internal packages (`internal/`) encapsulate selectors and accessibility, not exposed to consumers  
   - Examples act as “clients” validating API usability  

6. Drawing the System Design Diagram  
   a. Components as boxes:  
     - “Client App” (your code or examples)  
     - “huh Core” cluster:  
       • Form Manager (form.go, run.go)  
       • Groups & Fields (field_*.go, group.go)  
       • Options & Selector (option.go, internal/selector)  
       • Layout & Theme (layout.go, theme.go)  
       • Accessibility Renderer (accessibility.go, internal/accessibility)  
       • Validation (validate.go)  
     - “Spinner Module” cluster: spinner/spinner.go  
     - “External Libraries”: Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss, Go stdlib  
   b. Arrows for dependencies and data flow:  
     - Client App → imports → huh Core & spinner  
     - Form Manager → invokes → Groups & Fields → uses → Options & Selector  
     - Form Manager → Layout & Theme → Terminal Renderer  
     - Accessibility flag → toggles → Accessibility Renderer  
     - Client App (Bubble Tea) ↔ Form Manager (tea.Model Update/View)  
     - Spinner Module → Terminal Renderer  
   c. Architectural highlights:  
     - Show internal packages as shaded/grey boxes inside the core cluster  
     - Indicate the form lifecycle loop (Init → Update → View) with a circular arrow  
     - Depict optional path for Accessibility mode (dashed arrow from Form Manager to Accessibility Renderer)  
   d. Technologies & Frameworks labels:  
     - Go (module)  
     - Bubble Tea (optional integration)  
     - Lip Gloss (theme styling)  
     - Terminal / TTY  

7. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram  
   - Emphasize that this is a library architecture diagram, not a client/server network diagram.  
   - Highlight the API consumers (examples, client code) at the left, and the terminal I/O at the right.  
   - For the spinner, draw it as a separate module that clients call after completing the form.  

8. Diagram Styling Recommendations  
   - Use clear, concise labels on each box (e.g., “Form Manager”, “Field Types”)  
   - Use arrows with arrowheads to show call/invoke or dependency direction  
   - Color-code:  
     • Blue for public API components (Form, Fields)  
     • Grey for internal packages (internal/selector, internal/accessibility)  
     • Green for examples/clients  
     • Orange for external dependencies  
   - Use rounded rectangles for modules, diamonds for decision points (e.g., accessibility toggle), and circular arrows for loops  

By following this breakdown, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that captures the essential architecture of the “huh?” library, its spinner sub-package, and how clients interact with it. Ensure all major modules, data flows, and external integrations are represented, with clear labels, directional arrows, and consistent color coding.
